findings.input: A serving or training observation published by servingattempt.Record or trainingworkflow.Observer.finish when (a) the recipe-state read fails and the incoming Verification is empty, or (b) the same recipe is activated again, verified, after the recorded attempt executed it not verified.
findings.expected: Publication carries the state the executed recipe and task had at execution. A failed state read is told apart from a historical absent state and earns no verified credit, and a later activation does not replace execution-time state. Legacy bytes, the own-verifying-run exception and partial or cancelled results keep their contract.
findings.actual: The two remaining owners still read state at publication and drop the lookup error: servingattempt.Record (servingattempt.go:117-119) and Observer.finish (session_observation.go:271-273). A failed read leaves an empty Verification; scorecard.unverifiedAside rejects only explicit not-verified/broken and accepts that empty value as legacy. A later same-recipe activation is written as the attempt's state in place of its execution-time not-verified state. Shown from source at 8acbf71d17dfd3e1e35313b370f900b21f0fdf10; no SQA execution.

findings.input: (3) Gemma accuracy over 32 independent media, each with two uniformly guessed 3-choice questions. (4) Two judges ranked on all-constant finite scores, and on probabilities (.9,.1) against (.45,.45). (6) Two GIF media inputs for their own bound renders, with one judge and scorer, decoded at 16 frames against 1. (7) The embedded SenseNova APG verdict edited to 0 wins, 524 losses, 0 ties, 80 media and tail 0.0001, Admitted left true, with Says changed consistently to 'admitted: a gain beyond chance, 0 wins, 524 losses and 0 ties over 80 media'; its evaluation IDs stay unchanged. (8) A render campaign resumed after an earlier item's request changed while its last item drew the same, or with truncated bookkeeping.
findings.expected: (3) The accuracy null matches the actual choice counts and within-media dependence. (4) Ranking uses the aggregation production scores with, and an undefined tau or omitted resamples are said, without a panic. (6) A reading is admitted only from evaluations bound to the same render, decode sampling and question contract, and a control offers a candidate only by the admission for its own model, recipe and request. (7) The record's verdict, counts and tail are derived through AdmitPreset and its bound evaluations, so drift is refused. (8) A completed arm or verdict is reused only for the same bound inputs, evaluator and producer; changed work is refused or redone, and truncated bookkeeping does not count as complete.
findings.actual: (3) Correct count minus sum(1/choices) against zero is taken as a fair sign for ExactPairedBinary: a medium is positive with probability 5/9, and uniform guessing passes the 22-positive threshold (nominal tail 0.0250512) with probability 0.0914273, above the 0.05 level. (4) Arithmetic probability means rank (.9,.1) above (.45,.45), the reverse of production softShare's geometric mean; constant scores give a NaN tau, all 2000 resamples are dropped and resampledTau indexes an empty slice. (6) judgedRender compares content, request, producer, runtime and scorer but not MediaInput.Decode or the question contract, readRender never calls verifyRendered, ResolveActiveExecution takes the current activation, and the embedded offering uses recorded no-loss flags (plus a recorded gain for guidance methods) under a published model name/preset key, without runtime recipe/request binding. (7) The native record test checks evaluation-ID syntax, displayed counts and admitted/refused wording, but does not recompute Admitted or Tail through AdmitPreset and the bound evaluations. Gained trusts Tail <= falseGain, so the consistently worded false gain in input 7 passes the record and gain checks and offers APG on SenseNova's page despite its stated 524 losses and zero wins. (8) Arm, suite and verdict skips trust names and file existence and accept truncated bookkeeping, and a new build is validated by re-rendering only the last item. Remaining counterexamples shown from source and arithmetic at 0c24aca5b670940f95c0f8156c13804a9e2fd9ea; no SQA execution.

findings.input: A retained ClipMotion observation of unchanged MP4 bytes, then a motion encoder checkpoint or FFmpeg/preprocessing configuration changes under the same encoder basename. The suite is compiled again with that old observation and the same matching clip-content digest.
findings.expected: Motion readings identify the encoder/checkpoint and decoder/sampling contract that produced them, so changed instruments cannot silently reuse or be credited with an old metric. Keep the repaired OCR re-keying, content checks and whole-set exclusion in the existing media compiler and observation producers; the observation instrument is separate from the answering judge.
findings.actual: The remaining motion instrument is not bound: writeMotion passes filepath.Base(encoderPath) to measureMotion; ClipMotion stores that Encoder string and clip/source content digests, with no encoder/checkpoint or FFmpeg/sampling identity. ClipMotion.validate requires only a nonempty encoder name, and bindObservations compares clip.Content alone before keeping the motion set. Changing an instrument while the clip bytes and encoder basename stay the same therefore leaves the old motion admissible and its actual producing instrument indistinguishable. Shown from source at ba0405e63d92653b84f617d8c332d5546529e444; no SQA execution.

findings.input: On a case-insensitive Windows checkout, a task with Files [scripts] and Tests [scripts/held_test.go] whose worker calls edit_file or delete_file on scripts/HELD_test.go.
findings.expected: The worker's edit and delete tools must recognize the held test through either spelling and preserve its contents.
findings.actual: On a case-insensitive checkout, replay.go compares cleaned names with case-sensitive slices.Contains. The held test can therefore be edited or removed through the permitted directory. Source counterexample.

findings.input: Resume an accepted ComfyUI prompt after its model or installation changes, or keep two outputs from one node with the same basename in different subfolders.
findings.expected: Bind resumed output to its original producer, retain both files distinctly, and identify a peak sampled only after resume as a partial measurement.
findings.actual: record.go reads the current models and commits, then resumes on request hash and prompt ID alone. A completed older result can acquire the new producer metadata. await starts memory sampling at retry. keep fetches by subfolder but writes by node and basename, so the second output overwrites the first. These cases follow from source.

findings.input: Name a MOSS request while its required adapter is missing. Install the adapter before the draw opens it, then close the session, remove it and retry the same request.
findings.expected: Refuse a missing required adapter before replay or model work. Store an answer only under the identities of the files used to compute it. Preserve the single hash of a present, held adapter or depth checkpoint.
findings.actual: Contents records an absent dependency and continues. The draw can succeed under that key with the newly installed adapter. After removal the director can replay the result under the absent key. Source counterexample. Present adapters share a held identity across naming and execution.

findings.input: With all six standard recordings available, omit one floor declaration. Separately, put the first case below its floor and make a later recording fail to load or give that later case a hash-matching PNG of half the expected width. For the adapter check, give both precision modes a latent containing +Inf against a finite nonzero reference.
findings.expected: In moss-real-prompt/do, check every case has a floor before loading a generator. Report each failed comparison when scored and close that case's generator on every exit, before the next case. Require two valid latent comparisons for the adapter merge. Preserve +Inf for an exact finite match with nonzero signal.
findings.actual: holdGoldenFloors checks its declarations after six baseline draws and six controls. A later fatal error hides an earlier floor failure. A wrong-width PNG also makes pictureDecibels call Fatal before readGoldenCases reaches closeReporting, bypassing release of the generator and its directory hold. In holdMergedSections two invalid latents can pass as -Inf >= -Inf. These are source counterexamples. The passing 32cf1a5d0 models lane took 3m56s for the whole standard floor test, including its separate own-size draw.

findings.input: Complete and store a Wan clip. Restart with the same recipe, prompt and tokenizer after replacing the umT5 checkpoint with different compatible bytes at the same path, size and modification time.
findings.expected: A restart may reuse a stored clip only after establishing the current encoder's content identity.
findings.actual: TextPipelineIdentity accepts the memoized checkpoint digest on size and time. TestTextPipelineNamesItsCheckpointThroughTheStore expects the old identity after this replacement. The director can replay the old clip before loading the new encoder. Replay follows from source.

findings.input: After a passing needle-reference run, delete only fixtures/needle_upstream_calls.json and select lanes with -reached. The reader still names the old path. The same case applies to the models lane when only fixtures/moss/checkpoint.json is deleted.
findings.expected: CycleLanesReached selects the reader of the removed fixture, so the Needle or MOSS check reports the missing input. Use the existing reader lookup for deleted paths, or run the lane when its readers are unknown. Keep the current package selection for edits to existing fixtures.
findings.actual: Source trace at c71a1e230. The Git diff supplies the deleted path. TrackedDocuments lists only files still present, so documentReaders returns no entry. discover treats the missing entry as zero readers and omits the lane. Both checks fail on the missing file if selected. The retained gate verified selection for edits to both fixtures while they were present.

findings.input: In the existing mutantFixture, select a Go test that skips when Above(11) is false and otherwise passes. Above(v) returns v > 10. The baseline passes and reversing > to <= makes the only selected test skip.
findings.expected: Count failed Go assertions as caught and passing checks as survived. Report skips and builds that fail before any assertion as inconclusive, outside the catch-rate denominator.
findings.actual: mutate increments Refused for every verifier error. A mutant that makes the only test skip earns a catch through ErrVacuous. A failed build earns the same credit. Source counterexamples.

findings.input: Serve one 50-step MOSS text-to-image request with guidance 1, no skipped steps or adapters, and a fixed prompt such as 'red fox under pine trees' repeated 64 times.
findings.expected: Reuse the fixed branch's refined text on the device for the request. Preserve rotary positions, adapter settings and joint-block arithmetic. Check one refinement and identical seeded output across 50 steps.
findings.actual: compileRotaryDenoiserProgram includes textGraph.refine in the per-pass graph. Its prompt and weights are fixed, while only the later joint blocks consume the changing latent. The 50-step input therefore evaluates the same refinement 50 times. The count is source-derived. Time and peak-memory effects are unmeasured.

findings.input: Use an active MOSS image recipe, prompt 'a fox', 8 steps, an undeclared preset and a syntactically valid file ID for a missing source picture. Compare the request with no dimensions to the same request with width 1024 and height 576. Also try the explicit dimensions with a stored PNG and enhance enabled.
findings.expected: Both size forms should return the catalog's unknown-preset error before reading the picture or opening the enhancer. Have MOSS admission propagate the preset error its existing resolver already found. Preserve the content identity of admitted requests and fresh execution when only a reusable file identity is unavailable.
findings.actual: Source at d0eaf0f9a. With no dimensions, Sized resolves the preset and rejects it. Explicit dimensions bypass that lookup. Beside later returns the catalog error, but Reading retries as FreshRun. preparedFirst then returns the missing-picture error, or reads a stored PNG and invokes the enhancer for a request with an invalid preset. The landing's retained check verifies the original negative-step case with both stored and absent pictures.

findings.input: Draw the recorded 1024 by 576 MOSS depth-control section with 50 guided ER-SDE steps, control ending at 0.5 and scheduler shift 5. Both guidance branches request the same control at each step.
findings.expected: Select the resident control or zero buffer before constructing a host value. Allocate and upload zeros on the first use of that device slot only. Keep the same sigma boundary and seeded output.
findings.actual: controlAt creates a 64 x 36 x 256 float32 zero buffer before checking the resident slot. In the pass-2 recording 28 steps fall outside the window. Two branches create 56 buffers and only the first is uploaded. The other 55 account for 123.75 MiB of cumulative host allocation per draw, calculated from source and recorded sigmas. Wall time and peak memory are unmeasured.

findings.input: Complete a fixed-seed MOSS text-to-image request with Enhance enabled, then repeat it through the same local capability without FreshRun. Use the same store, code, model files, active recipe, source prompt and exclusions. The mode-2 recording supplies a source and its positive and negative outputs.
findings.expected: Recover the completed ordinary request before reopening the enhancer. Bind reuse to the enhancer model, tokenizer, template, sampling settings, code, picture inputs and current authority. FreshRun must still execute.
findings.actual: preparedFirst calls EnhanceRequest before the session director looks for a completed run. A retry opens the 9B chat and generates both prompts again, with another generation if the positive prompt needs a retry. A failed enhancer open prevents delivery of the stored picture. This follows from source. The retry was not timed.

findings.input: Run the MOSS adapter-transfer, INT8 kernel-budget, golden-floor and adapter-precision checks on the installed Ultra model.
findings.expected: Take cold and recurring-adapter bounds on the existing two traversals, including adapters reused within the first. Share one two-step census across both kernel budgets. For the adapter comparison draw each baseline once per precision. Keep the separate merge capture, both budget assertions and unexpected-kernel checks. Floor controls still need their changed latents. Decode only pictures a check consumes, and keep the full workflow clock.
findings.actual: The transfer tests draw 18 pictures for bounds available in 12. The two kernel budgets sample the same two steps twice. In the 32cf1a5d0 models run the two-traversal and one-traversal checks took 24.677 s and 16.651 s, and the product and attention checks took 5.734 s and 9.879 s. Separately, holdMergedSections calls readGoldenCases for three cases at two precisions and discards all six changed-input scores. The six standard and two Turbo floor controls also decode eight unused pictures. The counts follow from source. The reported times are process walls. Elapsed savings are unmeasured.

findings.input: Land a MOSS workflow timing record beside its plan and findings changes, as at 4586266fe. Also compare the two host stages of a15182b1b on the same MOSS landing.
findings.expected: Run the timing record's verifier and checks that consume the changed records. For identical inputs and build settings, execute each host suite once. Preserve the distinct whole-tree checks.
findings.actual: Timing-only landing 4586266fe took 8m55s, including 3m18.866s for invariants and 4m54.364s for tests. The fast path admits only the plan and findings. At a15182b1b the ordinary landing test TestALandingRefusesWhatDispatchWouldPass ran for 30s in invariants and 27s in the main test stage. The records do not identify individual cache misses.

findings.input: Dispatch an eligible MOSS step to a worker. While it runs, add an independent ready row that ranks ahead of it. Leave the assigned step, prerequisites, lane, scope and stop state unchanged. Land the original assignment.
findings.expected: Honor the step actually assigned through the existing dispatch owner while it is still eligible. Recheck its current terms, dependencies, lane and stops. An unrelated priority change should govern the next assignment.
findings.actual: AdmitLanding selects the first ready step again for a worker. An unrelated row moving ahead refuses a still-eligible assignment. Three logged refusals of moss-comfy-block/do named clock-committed/do, adapter-hold/do and moss-first-run/do. The selection rule follows from source. The log alone cannot establish each ranking change.

findings.input: Read the refusal worklist for moss-int8-epilogue/census on Nov 20. Its gate output names eight failing tests and subtests across capabilityruntime, audioparity and server.
findings.expected: The existing refusal worklist should attribute this landing once to each of the eight named tests and subtests. Preserve the complete failing names when classifying the gate result, with the short diagnostic kept separately from the counts. Older truncated records can establish only the names they actually retained.
findings.actual: Classify clips the cause to 240 bytes before refusedBy extracts names. The retained cause ends mid-name. Only TestNativeASRSessionAcceptance and TestSecondASRStreamingAcceptance/6930-75918-0000 reach the worklist. The full gate output retains all eight.

findings.input: Start the models lane with moss-elementwise/do (9acbc157a) after its last whole pass. The row selected three names across cuda/executor and latentimage. The first two tests exist only in executor and TestTheMOSSPassFusesWithoutChangingABit only in latentimage. All three have retained passes in their own packages after the row landed.
findings.expected: Rank each actual package and test pair using its own retained pass and the row commit. Keep a missing or stale pass first for that pair, including when two packages declare the same name. A passed pair still runs in its normal position in a whole lane. testSteps already lists each package's tests.
findings.actual: At f58916f2a, testsOfCheck attaches both packages to each name and passedSince requires a pass from both. No run can supply the three nonexistent pairs. The landing check supplies a synthetic pass for a test in a package that does not declare it. The 32cf1a5d0 lane passed the MOSS fusion draw in 16.754 s. Its pass was retained before the f58916f2a lane, which still ran that draw ahead of the checkpoint tests and spent 22.558 s on it. This is measured time before later checks, not a whole-lane speedup.

findings.input: For moss-real-prompt/do, record mode 3 at the existing 1024 by 576 canvas with 598.seed set to 7 and 450.high_level_description set to "red fox". Leave the section template at its committed seed of 69420 and empty description. Read that recording through the standard golden-floor check.
findings.expected: Build the comparison request from the inputs ComfyUI actually received. Apply the recorded node-input changes once in readComfySection before the case reads its sampler or builder. Check the reconstructed seed and description before drawing. Keep the rendered prompt previews and output hashes from that same recording.
findings.actual: The recorder updates both the posted request and recording.Set. readComfySection loads Set but inputs reads only the base template. textSection therefore uses seed 69420 and the mode-3 case builds an empty description, comparing a different draw to ComfyUI's output. The retained mode-3 recording illustrates the distinction: its selector is 3 while the template's is 1. The seed and description mismatch follows from source at bb918937d; no changed-input comparison was run.

findings.input: Start slow-whole/do in a clean checkout. While its models lane runs, start the row-close checks for the same commit, model inputs and machine. Interrupt the row-close process after named tests pass and before the models lane ends. Query those tests with validate -passed-since for that commit.
findings.expected: Use the full run for both obligations when their identities match. Keep completed individual passes queryable at their commit after interruption, using the existing pass record and batched writes. A partial run can answer individual test queries. Only a completed full run can satisfy slow-whole/do.
findings.actual: Only the row-close runner takes lanes.lock. At bb918937d both validators ran the same 325 package/test selections. Their summed test-process times were 74m37s in the row-close run and 74m29s in the full run. In 234 GPU waits naming only the full run, the row-close run waited 57m30s. It exited after 2h42m22s with only exit status 1. Ten explicit passes (57m19s of test time) still queried at older commits after exit, including both MOSS checkpoints. executeMeasured buffers reports until keepLaneRun at lane end. The full run subsequently published those passes. The measured times describe separate runs and waits; end-to-end savings are unmeasured.

findings.input: Run slow-whole/do from a clean linked checkout with valid data roots and no local-models.json. TestLandedStepsReplayForAWorker prepares its child checkout through moveWithRoots. A second case uses a checkout-relative models override with no environment override.
findings.expected: Use the caller's effective data roots in the replay checkout and historical checks. dataroot.ResolveEnvironment already binds those roots for validateTo. Preserve explicit overrides and errors for invalid settings. The optional file's absence should require no manual copy, and a relative path should keep identifying the same directory.
findings.actual: At bb918937d the full run passed four of five lanes. Its sole named failure was TestLandedStepsReplayForAWorker: after 23.56s it reported that the clean checkout's local-models.json was missing (replay_windows_model_test.go:47). moveWithRoots moves the tree, then requires the ignored file, although dataroot.Resolve accepts its absence. When the file exists, copying its bytes also resolves a relative override against the child directory. That second case follows from source. The checkout contained a copy after the recorded failure.

SQA-459.note: Answered by the lead on 2026-11-22 at bb918937d: valid, met in slow-whole/do's run (TestLandedStepsReplayForAWorker failed after 23.56 s on the clean checkout's missing local-models.json, moveWithRoots requiring the ignored file dataroot.Resolve does without; with the trunk's copied in, the models lane cut to cmd/loop passed its 82 tests, the replay in 32.6 s).
